title: Palindromic Substring Count
statement:
Count how many substrings of a string are palindromes, counting each position range separately.

Contract
- `text` is non-null, may be empty, and has length at most 50,000. Characters are compared
  exactly (case-sensitive).
- A substring is identified by its start and end positions, so equal substrings found at
  different positions are counted separately. Single characters are palindromes.
- Return the total count. For an empty `text` the count is `0`.

Examples
- `countPalindromes("abc")` returns `3` (`a`, `b`, `c`).
- `countPalindromes("aaa")` returns `6` (three `a`, two `aa`, one `aaa`).
- `countPalindromes("abba")` returns `6` (`a`, `b`, `b`, `a`, `bb`, `abba`).
hints: Every palindrome has a middle: one character for odd lengths, or the gap between two characters for even lengths.
From each of the 2n - 1 centers, expand outward while the two ends match; every successful expansion is one more palindromic substring.
Add one to the total per successful expansion; no extra storage is needed. Intended complexity: O(n^2) time and O(1) extra space, where n is the length of the text.
inputSyntax: Input: one piece of text with no spaces, for example: abba
